claims.claim: I tested it myself yesterday, everything I said is true
claims.evidence: Seller’s testing claim is not verifiable without new photos/video showing the wardrobe functioning and condition.

risks.risk: Hidden stains/tears on fabric panels or seams not visible because the wardrobe is packed in the photo.
risks.proof: Request 2–3 close-up photos of each fabric panel/seam (front, sides, and inside corners) with items removed.
risks.if_unproven: Price as used with possible minor fabric wear (worst case: stains/tears present).

risks.risk: Missing/loose parts (zippers, connectors, poles, shelf ties) or weak frame joints.
risks.proof: Request a short video showing the wardrobe being assembled/standing stable, plus close-ups of all joints/connectors.
risks.if_unproven: Price as needing repair/parts if any are missing (worst case: not fully functional).

risks.risk: Odor (smoke, dampness) that isn’t detectable from the single photo.
risks.proof: Ask for a photo/video of the wardrobe being aired out and a quick odor check clip.
risks.if_unproven: Price as if odor may be present (worst case: requires cleaning/airing).

risks.risk: Foam firmness claim may refer to padding that isn’t visible; could be sagging or damaged.
risks.proof: Request close-up photos of any foam/padded sections (if present) and a hand-press/rebound clip.
risks.if_unproven: Price as if foam is not firm/unknown condition (worst case: foam worn).

proof_requests: Send close-up photos of all fabric panels and seams (front, sides, inside corners) with items removed.
Send a short video showing the wardrobe standing stable and fully usable (open/close, hanging rail, shelf sections).
Show any foam/padded parts clearly (if present) with a hand-press/rebound clip.
Provide proof of purchase date (receipt or message) if claiming 'bought new last year'.
response.reason: The seller insists the claims are true, but without new photos/video the key condition points (no stains/tears, foam firmness, smoke-free) remain unverified from the current single packed image. Worst-case pricing still requires proof.
